title: Hedge funds report using agents for research while restricting autonomy
dek: Firms describe research augmentation and process automation but emphasize security isolation and the risk of passive analytical dependence.
evidence: Industry executive interviews and reporting; no comparable audited fund performance study
takeaway: Measure agent-aided research quality and analyst independence, not just the volume of automated outputs.

sections.title: Operating patterns

bullets.detail: Reported examples include independent agent-assisted research preparation, codified research processes and reduction of routine analyst work.
Executives stressed narrow environments and human control for agents that could touch sensitive systems, investment decisions or trading workflows.

paragraphs: Research: Reported examples include independent agent-assisted research preparation, codified research processes and reduction of routine analyst work.
Boundaries: Executives stressed narrow environments and human control for agents that could touch sensitive systems, investment decisions or trading workflows.

sections.title: Evidence and tests

bullets.detail: An assistant that generates plausible theses can cause analysts to inherit unsupported assumptions; workflow productivity is not a demonstrated investment alpha.
Compare idea novelty, citation fidelity, methodological challenge rate, analyst disagreement and post-trade attribution; keep portfolio decisions under explicit authorized controls.
